program.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
requirements.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.

nodes.question: Has the image been transformed into a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: complete: the image is a chalk drawing; partial: some visible progress toward making it a chalk drawing, but it is not complete; absent: no requested change has progressed; unknown: evidence is insufficient to determine progress or completion. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Target: the image. Reference: a drawing made from chalk.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

decomposition_error: ValueError: Only ancestor evidence references and depth <= four are supported

broad.reason: The single direct-image check covers the full requested transformation—turning the image into a chalk drawing—and distinguishes complete fulfillment, partial progress, no progress, and insufficient evidence. It adds no unrelated constraints or mandatory techniques, and the aggregation has one applicable outcome.
